question: A 6-month-old male baby comes with vomiting, lethargy and severe jaundice when weaning was staed with fruit juice. Which of the following enzymes is defective?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Introduction of fruit juice" -> "ingestion of fructose" -> "defective metabolism of fructose" -> "accumulation of toxic metabolites" -> "vomiting, lethargy, severe jaundice" -> "Aldolase B deficiency" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Introduction of fruit juice" -> "ingestion of fructose" -> "normal metabolism of fructose by Fructokinase" -> "no accumulation of toxic metabolites" -> "unlikely cause of symptoms" -> "Fructokinase not defective" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Introduction of fruit juice" -> "ingestion of sucrose" -> "Sucrase required for sucrose breakdown" -> "normal function of Sucrase" -> "no direct link to severe jaundice" -> "Sucrase not defective" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Introduction of fruit juice" -> "ingestion of fructose" -> "Aldolase A involved in glycolysis, not fructose metabolism" -> "no direct involvement in fructose breakdown" -> "Aldolase A not defective" -> 90%
analysis: The symptoms described in the question - vomiting, lethargy, and severe jaundice upon introduction of fruit juice - suggest a metabolic issue related to the breakdown of fructose. Aldolase B is an enzyme crucial in the fructose metabolism pathway, specifically in the liver. Deficiency in Aldolase B leads to hereditary fructose intolerance (HFI), which manifests when fructose or sucrose (which contains fructose) is introduced into the diet. This condition can lead to severe symptoms including hypoglycemia, vomiting, jaundice, and even liver failure if not managed by dietary restrictions. The other enzymes listed (Fructokinase, Aldolase A, and Sucrase) do not lead to the severe symptoms observed in this scenario when deficient. Fructokinase deficiency leads to essential fructosuria, a benign condition. Aldolase A deficiency affects glycolysis but is not typically associated with fructose ingestion. Sucrase deficiency would affect sucrose breakdown but does not typically result in severe jaundice or hypoglycemia.
